gap: No result ChatGPT got points out that the watt figures on these amps are measured under different conditions. Dayton rates the SPA250DSP at 250 W RMS into 4 Ω at under 0.1% THD+N. Behringer gives the NX3000D's 900 W/1,500 W per channel with no conditions at all. TI rates the TPA3255 chip at 10% THD+N (600 W) and only 480 W at 1%. The Fosi M03's own page gives 200 W RMS and 150 W RMS for the same 4 Ω load, and its 32 V/5 A power brick is rated 160 W, so it can't supply the 200 W spec.
standout_why: ChatGPT's answer cited the two B&H compare pages. Both returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch, so I couldn't check what they say about rating conditions. Going by the answer as shown and the retailer and distributor pages that came up, the NX3000D, XLS 1002 and SPA250DSP all appear as bare watt figures. ChatGPT calls the NX3000D a '1,500-watt' amp, which is Behringer's 2 Ω figure, and it compares that number against Crown's 4 Ω number. It tells the shopper to go by RMS rather than peak, but it never says that one of its three picks has no stated conditions and another has fixed ones. The Fosi M03 is the amp Dealectric lists, and none of the results mention it or its power-supply limit.
decides: This confirms the dedicated-amp picks but changes how to size them. Read the power figure at the sub's own impedance, and trust it only when the conditions are given. Dayton's 250 W into 4 Ω at under 0.1% THD+N is the only one of the three cards with stated conditions. The NX3000D's 900 W/ch into 4 Ω (not 1,500 W) has none, so treat it as headroom rather than a guaranteed continuous figure. For the Fosi M03 as shipped, size to the 150 W RMS into 4 Ω figure. That makes it a match for subs rated about 150 W or less. Getting near 200 W needs a stronger supply than the 32 V/5 A brick, within the 24–48 V input range.

My arithmetic, using the page's own figures.

findings.note: Behringer's product page gives no 8 Ω figure. ChatGPT's '1,500-watt' card uses the 2 Ω figure. Most home passive subs are 4 Ω or 8 Ω, and at 4 Ω the stated figure is 900 W/ch.
